reason: Quote and mechanism are exact. TabListManager.java:491 computes `int frame = (int) ((tick / Math.max(1, line.frameTicks())) % frames.size());` from `tick`, and `tick` is only ever mutated at line 343 `tick++;` inside refreshAllUnchecked (grep over the whole class shows occurrences only at 123, 124, 303, 343, 491 — no rescaling, no add of the period). The task that drives it is scheduled at line 159 `refreshTask = Bukkit.getScheduler().runTaskTimer(plugin, this::refreshAll, period, period);` with `int period = tab.refreshTicks() > 0 ? tab.refreshTicks() : DisplayConfig.DEFAULT_TAB_REFRESH_TICKS;` (line 149), and DisplayConfig.DEFAULT_TAB_REFRESH_TICKS = 20 (DisplayConfig.java:120), matching the shipped `tab.refresh-ticks: 20` (src/main/resources/display.yml:137). So one refresh = 20 ticks, one `tick` increment = 20 ticks, and a frame change requires frameTicks increments = frameTicks*20 ticks: with frame-ticks 20 a frame lasts 400 ticks (20 s), not the documented 1 s — exactly the claimed 20x. The unit contract is explicit and shared by both renderers: display.yml:32 `frame-ticks: <tick> 仅 anim：每帧持续 tick 数，1-200（20 tick = 1 秒）`, DisplayConfig.java:48 `@param frameTicks 仅 ANIM：每帧 tick 数 [1,200]`, and TabListManager.java:123 itself calls `tick` a 'tick 计数'. ArenaScoreboard does the same job correctly — `tickCounter += refreshPeriodTicks;` (ArenaScoreboard.java:383) with the period loaded from scoreboard.refresh-ticks (line 325) and the identical frame formula at line 616 — so the tab path is an off-by-unit bug, not a deliberate different semantic; the doc/field comments give no definition of frame-ticks as 'refresh frames'. Header/footer lines go through the same parseLine (DisplayConfigLoader.java:188-191, 248) so `anim` really is accepted there. Severity stays medium rather than high: the failure is purely cosmetic (animation cadence), the shipped layout contains no anim line (display.yml:145-152 are static keys; the anim example at lines 69-71 is commented out), and an admin can partially compensate with frame-ticks: 1 — but the behavior still contradicts the documented unit and couples animation speed to tab.refresh-ticks.
